name: Tulfes
kurzbeschreibung: Nestled between the slopes of the Glungezer and the Patscherkofel—a peaceful retreat with stunning mountain views.
beschreibung:
Overview

Tulfes is situated at an elevation of 923 meters on a sunny high terrace in the southeastern Mittelgebirge south of the Inn Valley, nestled at the foot of Mount Glungezer (2,677 meters). With roughly 1,700 residents, this peaceful Tyrolean village lies about six kilometers southeast of the historic salt town of Hall in Tirol and twelve kilometers east of Innsbruck. Thanks to its elevated vantage point, visitors take in sweeping views across the valley floor to the jagged limestone cliffs of the Nordkette in the Karwendel range. Tulfes has preserved its authentic farming heritage with centuries-old timber farmsteads, making it a serene year-round haven for families, hikers, and nature enthusiasts away from mass tourism.

History

Bronze Age archaeological artifacts reveal that this sunlit terrace was inhabited more than 2,500 years ago. Tulfes was first documented in 1266 as 'Tulphes', a pre-Roman toponym describing flower-strewn mountain slopes. In the village center stands the Parish Church of Saint Thomas: first recorded in 1332, the sanctuary was rebuilt in Late Gothic style in 1486. In the early 18th century, the church tower was crowned with its distinctive Baroque onion dome and trompe-l'œil facade murals, complemented inside by an ornate high altar from 1724 and an exterior 16th-century Saint Christopher fresco. During the 20th century, Mount Glungezer became an established regional recreation peak. Tulfes also preserves the singular tradition of 'Klumpern'—a heritage winter sport raced on single-runner wooden toboggans with a central handle, celebrated as living folklore and a popular weekly competition.

Getting There

By car, Tulfes is reached via the Inntal Autobahn A12 by taking the Hall-Mitte or Hall-Ost exit and following state road L38 uphill for roughly eight minutes. From Innsbruck, an alternative scenic route leads via Aldrans and Rinn. Train passengers arrive at Hall in Tirol railway station or Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof. Regular VVT bus line 540 provides frequent connections linking Innsbruck, Rinn, Tulfes, and Hall in Tirol.

Tips

A premier family destination is the Kugelwald on Mount Glungezer at the Halsmarter mid-station (1,560 meters): covering 8,000 square meters, it ranks as the world's largest alpine wooden marble run, weaving through ancient Swiss stone pine woods with treehouses and play stations. Hikers should not miss the panoramic Zirbenweg trail, winding at 2,000 meters through Europe's oldest contiguous stone pine forest between Patscherkofel and the Tulfeinalm. The modern Glungezer cable car ascends to the Tulfein top station (2,055 meters), serving as the springboard to the Glungezerhütte alpine lodge.
